title_en: Opinions of the Supreme People's Court and the China Disabled Persons' Federation on Effectively Protecting the Legitimate Rights and Interests of Persons with Disabilities in Trial and Enforcement Work
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court  China Disabled Persons' Federation

Opinions on Effectively Protecting the Lawful Rights and Interests of Persons with Disabilities in Trial and Enforcement Work

Fa Fa [2018] No. 15

Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; Disabled Persons' Federations of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Disabled Persons' Federation of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps; and the Disabled Persons' Federation of the Heilongjiang Reclamation Area:

Persons with disabilities are a special group facing difficulties in society and require extraordinary care and enhanced protection from the whole society. Effectively protecting the lawful rights and interests of persons with disabilities is an important mission for the People's Courts to thoroughly implement the spirit of the 19th National Congress of the Communist Party of China and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and to adhere to the principles of putting people first and administering justice for the people. To substantially safeguard the lawful rights and interests of persons with disabilities and facilitate their participation in litigation activities, the following opinions are put forward in accordance with the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Persons with Disabilities and other legal provisions.

1. Basic Requirements. People's Courts shall, in accordance with the principles of facilitating litigation for both parties and the national laws and policies on protecting persons with disabilities, adhere to a problem-oriented approach, adopt measures tailored to individual cases, actively respond to the judicial needs of persons with disabilities, ensure that persons with disabilities can participate equally, fully, and conveniently in litigation activities, and continuously improve the capacity and level of providing judicial services and guarantees for persons with disabilities. Disabled Persons' Federations shall perform their duties according to law and actively provide support and assistance to persons with disabilities for their participation in litigation activities.

2. Strengthening Communication and Coordination. When handling cases involving persons with disabilities, communication and liaison with Disabled Persons' Federations and other people's organizations, relevant government departments, as well as the work units, communities, residents' committees, and villagers' committees of the persons with disabilities shall be strengthened to fully understand the situation, fully communicate and coordinate, promote the resolution of the actual difficulties faced by the parties with disabilities, and work together to protect the lawful rights and interests of persons with disabilities.

3. Facilitating Case Filing for Persons with Disabilities. For cases involving persons with disabilities where transportation is inconvenient, the People's Tribunals may directly accept the case for filing; actively adopt green channels such as online case filing, door-to-door case filing, and telephone case filing for rapid case filing. If a person with disabilities has genuine difficulty in writing a statement of complaint, an oral complaint may be made, which shall be recorded in the笔录 by the People's Court; if the submitted statement of complaint has deficiencies or errors, the content requiring correction shall be fully informed at one time, along with guidance.

4. Strengthening Litigation Guidance. For parties with disabilities, guidance and explanation on litigation procedures shall be strengthened to ensure they exercise their litigation rights according to law. For parties with disabilities who have genuine difficulty in collecting evidence on their own, the conditions for the court to investigate and collect evidence of its own authority shall be appropriately relaxed according to law. For parties with disabilities applying for preservation, the method of preservation guarantee shall be reasonably determined according to law based on the specific circumstances of the case and the actual situation of the party with disabilities.

5. Applying the Guardianship System According to Law. When a person with disabilities who lacks or has limited capacity for civil conduct participates in litigation, their guardian shall act as the statutory agent to represent them in the litigation. If no guardian has been previously designated, persons eligible for guardianship may negotiate to determine a guardian. If negotiation fails, a guardian shall be designated from among persons legally eligible for guardianship in accordance with the principle of the best interests of the ward and respecting the true wishes of the ward. If there is no person legally eligible for guardianship, a relevant organization may be designated as the litigation agent in accordance with the provisions of Article 32 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China.

6. Facilitating Participation in Litigation. A relatively flexible trial working mechanism shall be adopted to facilitate the participation of persons with disabilities in litigation. Extensively promote circuit trial modes such as vehicle-mounted courts, on-site trials, and door-to-door mediation, and strive to conclude cases in court and resolve disputes on the spot. Fully utilize information technology means, using remote video methods such as online court hearings and online mediation to facilitate litigation for parties with disabilities.

7. Accelerating the Trial Process. For cases involving parties with disabilities, streamline the process by separating simple from complex cases according to law to improve litigation efficiency. Hold hearings early, render judgments promptly, and conclude cases as soon as possible to shorten the case handling cycle. Fully utilize the small claims procedure, leveraging the advantages of final adjudication at first instance to promptly realize the lawful rights and interests of parties with disabilities. For monetary payment cases where the facts are clear and the creditor-debtor relationship is definite, guide parties with disabilities to apply for the supervision procedure according to law to obtain a quick conclusion via an order for payment. For claims for alimony, support, child support, pension, medical expenses, labor remuneration, and immediate restitution of social insurance funds or social assistance funds, grant advance execution according to law.

8. Strengthening Enforcement Efforts. For cases won by parties with disabilities, if the party concerned fails to perform voluntarily, the case shall be directly transferred for enforcement, promptly entering the enforcement procedure. Enforcement efforts shall be intensified, and the case shall be concluded quickly according to law, ensuring the timely realization of the lawful rights and interests of persons with disabilities.

9. Strengthening Legal Aid. Within three days from the date of accepting a criminal case, inform the defendant with disabilities according to law of their right to entrust a defender; if they have not entrusted a defender due to financial difficulties or other reasons, inform them to apply for legal aid to the local legal aid institution or to apply for legal assistance to the local Disabled Persons' Federation. For victims with disabilities in criminal cases, private prosecutors with disabilities, and parties with disabilities in civil and administrative cases who have not entrusted a litigation agent due to financial difficulties, inform them that they may apply for legal aid to the local legal aid institution or apply for legal assistance to the local Disabled Persons' Federation. Upon receiving an application for legal aid from a party with disabilities, it shall be promptly forwarded to the legal aid institution according to law.

10. Strengthening Judicial Aid. For parties with disabilities who have genuine financial difficulties and meet the relevant conditions, court fees shall be deferred, reduced, or exempted according to law. For persons with disabilities who meet the conditions for judicial aid, inform them that they have the right to apply for aid. For parties with disabilities who have already received legal aid, judicial aid shall be granted.

11. Timely Designation of Defense Counsel. If a criminal defendant is a minor with disabilities, or an adult with disabilities who is blind, deaf, mute, or unable to fully recognize or control their own conduct, or a person with disabilities who may be sentenced to life imprisonment or death, and has not entrusted a defender, the legal aid institution shall be notified according to law to assign a lawyer to provide defense.

12. Severely Punishing Crimes Against Persons with Disabilities. For crimes infringing upon the rights and interests of persons with disabilities, especially crimes such as forcing persons with disabilities to work by means of violence, threats, or restricting personal freedom; organizing persons with disabilities to beg by means of violence or coercion; and organizing minor persons with disabilities to engage in theft, fraud, robbery, extortion, and other activities violating public security administration, impose severe punishment according to law to effectively protect the personal and property safety of persons with disabilities.

13. Imposing Lenient Sentences on Defendants with Disabilities According to Law. For defendants with disabilities in criminal cases, where the criminal circumstances are minor and punishment by criminal penalty is not necessary according to law, a sentence may be exempted from criminal punishment; for mentally ill persons who have not completely lost the ability to recognize or control their own conduct and commit crimes, a lighter or mitigated punishment may be imposed; for persons who are both deaf and mute, or blind persons who commit crimes, a lighter, mitigated, or exempted punishment may be imposed.

14. Handling State Compensation Cases Filed by Persons with Disabilities. For cases where persons with disabilities apply for state compensation, treat various rights claims raised by persons with disabilities seriously; if the conditions for acceptance are met, accept the case promptly according to law. Fully listen to the opinions of persons with disabilities regarding the method of compensation, items of compensation, and amount of compensation, and make a compensation decision promptly according to law.

15. Improving the Diverse Dispute Resolution Mechanism for Disputes Involving Persons with Disabilities. For civil cases involving persons with disabilities, actively carry out pre-litigation mediation, entrusted mediation, and diverse mediation, and vigorously leverage the forces of organizations such as Disabled Persons' Federations, People's Mediation Committees, grassroots judicial offices, and relevant departments such as public security and traffic, labor security, and medical health to jointly resolve disputes.

16. Giving Full Play to the Role of Judicial Suggestions. If during trial and enforcement work it is discovered that a relevant unit has infringed upon the rights and interests of persons with disabilities or has inadequately performed its duties in protecting the rights of persons with disabilities, the situation shall be promptly reported to the relevant unit as well as the local government's competent department and the Disabled Persons' Federation; if necessary, issue judicial suggestions, and track feedback and supervise implementation.

17. Properly Handling Petition Cases Involving Persons with Disabilities According to Law. For petitioning parties with disabilities, the People's Court shall provide special care, receive them promptly, and respond to any petition. Carefully review the petition materials, listen to opinions, and promptly record the visitor's information. For questions that can be answered on the spot, answer immediately; for questions that cannot be answered on the spot, inform them to wait for processing within the prescribed period.

18. Improving Barrier-Free Facilities and Services for Litigation. Vigorously promote the construction of barrier-free facilities in court reception areas and trial areas to facilitate the participation of persons with disabilities in litigation. Actively promote the construction of an accessible environment for information exchange; according to the circumstances of the case, allow relevant auxiliary and accompanying personnel to accompany the party with disabilities to appear in court.

19. Supporting Disabled Persons' Federations in Performing Their Duties According to Law. Disabled Persons' Federations shall actively help persons with disabilities obtain legal services. If a Disabled Persons' Federation receives an application for legal assistance, it shall handle it according to laws and regulations. A Disabled Persons' Federation may, upon request, assist a person with disabilities in applying to the People's Court for judicial aid.

20. Disabled Persons' Federations shall proactively undertake the duty of providing legal assistance services to persons with disabilities, and actively cooperate with and support the People's Courts in handling cases involving persons with disabilities. Disabled Persons' Federations shall actively conduct litigation guidance, answer questions, explain the law, and clarify reasoning for parties with disabilities.

21. Disabled Persons' Federations and Legal Assistance Workstations for Persons with Disabilities may proactively support persons with disabilities whose civil rights and interests have been harmed, disability organizations, and disability service institutions in filing lawsuits with the People's Court according to law; they may participate in litigation activities such as circuit trials, online court hearings, on-site mediation, and online mediation according to law, providing necessary assistance and support to parties with disabilities.

22. Disabled Persons' Federations shall proactively cooperate with the People's Courts to contact and hire auxiliary personnel to provide litigation auxiliary services such as sign language and braille for parties with disabilities, facilitating the participation of persons with disabilities in litigation activities.

July 13, 2018
